issues.description: The introduction states that the resistance interventions will be placed before collaborative recall, but the Method procedure places them after collaborative recall and immediately before the individual memory test. This is a central design feature because pre-exposure inoculation and post-exposure warning target different mechanisms and have different theoretical interpretations.
issues.quote: "What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation)."

issues.description: The Procedure explicitly presents collaborative recall, including misinformation exposure, before the interventions. This contradicts the earlier rationale that interventions are intended to inoculate participants before misinformation can take effect. The inconsistency makes the planned causal mechanism and analysis difficult to evaluate.
issues.quote: "The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation (and a control condition), and (4) an individual memory test of the original material."

issues.subcategory: extended warning content impossible if administered before discussion
issues.description: The extended warning is described as explaining that the partner saw a different movie version and why deception was applied. If delivered before collaborative recall, this would reveal the MORI manipulation and likely alter the discussion itself; if delivered after discussion, it is a post-warning rather than inoculation. The manuscript fails to resolve this incompatibility.
issues.quote: "Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied, should make the participants who are aware of discrepancies discard the consistency assumption"

issues.description: The Method says the final individual memory test will contain open-ended questions, but the Analysis plan later says the individual memory test will use a two-alternative forced-choice format. These formats yield different outcome distributions, guessing rates, scoring rules, and comparability to prior MORI work.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie"

issues.description: The Analysis plan contradicts the Procedure by stating that the individual memory test will use two-alternative forced-choice questions. The scoring system and planned ANOVA cannot be evaluated without a consistent measurement format.
issues.quote: "In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format."

issues.subcategory: open-ended modification contradicted by forced-choice description
issues.description: The Analysis plan first states that the study modifies prior MORI work by using open-ended questions, but then describes forced-choice scoring. This internal contradiction affects construct validity, comparability to the power analysis, and the definition of misinformation-consistent answers.
issues.quote: "First we will examine the memory conformity effect using the procedure of Garry et al. (2008; also Ito et al., 2019), but with modification concerning applying open-ended questions in the individual memory test."

issues.description: Participants are tested in dyads and exchange misinformation with each other, so their outcomes are statistically dependent. The planned two-factor ANOVA appears to treat individuals as independent observations and does not model pair/dyad as a clustering factor or random effect. Ignoring dyadic non-independence can underestimate standard errors and inflate Type I error.
issues.quote: "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels"

issues.description: The power analysis is based on individual participant counts, but randomization and discussion occur at the pair level. Effective sample size is closer to the number of dyads for between-condition comparisons, and within-dyad correlations should be accounted for. This may make the intervention comparisons substantially less powered than claimed.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)."

issues.subcategory: inappropriate ANOVA for bounded count outcomes
issues.description: The primary outcomes are counts out of a small number of critical items, likely 0–4 per condition or 0–8 overall, with bounded, discrete, non-normal distributions. A conventional ANOVA on counts or proportions may be inappropriate, especially with ceiling/floor effects. A binomial or multinomial mixed-effects model at the item level would better match the data structure.
issues.quote: "We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers."

issues.description: Only eight critical details are used, with four discussed and four non-discussed. Responses are nested within participants and items, and item difficulty may differ. The proposed participant-level ANOVA does not model item effects or item-by-condition variability, limiting generalization beyond the specific items.
issues.quote: "Both versions are identical except for eight critical details"

issues.subcategory: low number of trials per condition
issues.description: The conformity effect and intervention interaction are estimated from only four discussed and four non-discussed critical items per participant. Such small trial counts produce noisy individual estimates and reduce reliability, particularly for interactions among four groups.
issues.quote: "the participants will discuss half of the dissimilar details they have seen"

issues.subcategory: power analysis based on unstable meta-analysis
issues.description: The memory conformity power analysis combines only two highly heterogeneous effect sizes, Hedges' g = 1.92 and 0.38, to derive a joint effect of 1.13. With only two studies and large heterogeneity, the pooled estimate is highly unstable and should not be treated as a reliable planning value.
issues.quote: "Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13."

issues.subcategory: effect-size conversion unclear or likely incorrect
issues.description: The manuscript states that Hedges' g = 1.13 amounts to Cohen's f of about 0.57 for a repeated-measures comparison. This conversion is not explained and may not be appropriate for a within-subject design, where standardized mean differences depend on the within-person correlation and variance metric used.
issues.quote: "This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57."

issues.subcategory: questionable use of repeated-measures correlation in power analysis
issues.description: The authors assume r = .07 between discussed and non-discussed scores based on prior work. A near-zero correlation is unusual for repeated measures of memory accuracy and may reflect noisy estimates from few items rather than a stable planning parameter. Power calculations for within-subject effects and interactions are sensitive to this value.
issues.quote: "The joint correlation of results in the discussed and non-discussed items in both studies available was 0.07."

issues.subcategory: directional tests not justified or specified
issues.description: The manuscript states that directional significance tests are assumed, but several interventions are acknowledged as possibly increasing conformity. Directional tests are inappropriate when plausible effects exist in both directions, and the exact alpha level and test implementation are not specified.
issues.quote: "Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed."

issues.description: The analysis includes four outcome indices, accuracy on filler/non-discussed/discussed questions, interaction tests, pairwise comparisons, confidence ratings, awareness analyses, and DRM predictors. No plan is provided for controlling familywise error or false discovery, increasing risk of selective significant findings.
issues.quote: "We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices"

issues.description: Pairwise intervention comparisons are planned only if the omnibus interaction is significant. This gatekeeping strategy may be underpowered and does not specify the exact planned contrasts most relevant to the hypotheses, such as each intervention versus control and ordering among interventions.
issues.quote: "In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed."

issues.description: The interventions are assumed to increase warning comprehension, memory knowledge, motivation, or vulnerability awareness, but no manipulation checks are described. Without measuring whether participants understood or internalized the interventions, null or positive results cannot be interpreted mechanistically.
issues.quote: "The main goal of this proposal is to analyze the efficacy of three possible methods of reducing memory conformity. These are (1) Extended warning against misinformation, (2) providing detailed knowledge about the fallibility of memory ... and (3) demonstrating the vulnerability of memory and motivating subjects to overcome it"

issues.subcategory: control condition not matched to interventions
issues.description: The control podcast concerns soft skills related to social attitudes and may not match the intervention conditions in relevance, arousal, perceived importance, threat, legal framing, memory focus, or demand characteristics. The DRM condition also includes an active task and feedback, unlike the podcast-only conditions. Differences may reflect attention, engagement, affect, or demand rather than the intended mechanisms.
issues.quote: "In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes."

issues.description: Extended warning and education are approximately 7-minute podcasts, whereas demonstration and motivation includes a DRM task, feedback, and a motivational podcast. The duration and cognitive load appear unequal, creating confounds in comparisons among interventions.
issues.quote: "First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used"

issues.description: The experimenter administers interventions, collaborative recall, DRM feedback, and final testing, but there is no description of blinding to condition or hypotheses. Experimenter expectancy could influence instructions, feedback, interaction tone, or coding.
issues.quote: "At this moment in this group, the experimenter will give the following information to the participants"

issues.description: Open-ended answers and audio-recorded discussions require coding, but no blinding of coders to condition or participants' viewed version is specified. Unblinded coding can bias classification of responses as correct, misinformation-consistent, or other.
issues.quote: "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers"

issues.description: If open-ended responses and collaborative-recall misinformation exposure are coded, the manuscript does not specify the number of coders, coding rules, adjudication procedures, or reliability statistics. This limits replicability and confidence in outcome classification.
issues.quote: "The discussion will be audio recorded."

issues.subcategory: all dyads discuss same critical items
issues.description: The manuscript says discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but later states that every pair will discuss the same four critical details. If true, item status is confounded with item identity: differences between discussed and non-discussed items could reflect item difficulty or memorability rather than misinformation exposure.
issues.quote: "In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase."

issues.description: The Design section claims full counterbalancing of discussed and non-discussed items, but the Procedure states that the same set of four critical details will always be discussed. These cannot both be true. This directly affects the internal validity of the within-subject comparison.
issues.quote: "discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced"

issues.description: The analysis says all discussed items will be categorized as containing misinformation because the procedure is designed to expose participants to differing versions. But actual exposure depends on what the partner said. If the partner guessed the participant's version, said 'don't know,' or failed to mention the critical detail, coding the item as misinformation exposure is invalid and dilutes or biases the effect.
issues.quote: "we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s differing version of events."

issues.description: The Analysis plan first says partner answers matching the participant's version or 'don't know' will not be classified as misleading, but immediately afterward says all discussed items will be categorized as containing misinformation. These scoring rules conflict.
issues.quote: "However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen ... the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer ‘don’t know’ will also not be classified as misleading."

issues.description: For forced-choice scoring, any partner response inconsistent with the participant's version, including responses inconsistent with both movie versions, is classified as misleading. This conflates co-witness misinformation specific to the partner's viewed event with generic errors, guesses, or conversational noise.
issues.quote: "All the answers provided by the partner during the discussion (green mug, violet mug, yellow mug, blue mug) are misleading the participant and will be classified as misleading."

issues.description: The procedure says both responses will be documented if participants cannot agree, but does not specify whether both participants are still considered exposed to misinformation, how disagreement affects coding, or how dominance and source monitoring are handled analytically.
issues.quote: "If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented."

issues.description: The manuscript states that pairs will be randomly assigned to conditions, but does not specify allocation method, concealment, blocking, stratification by sex/age/familiarity, or assignment of movie versions/glasses. In dyadic social influence studies, imbalance in these factors can confound results.
issues.quote: "Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups"

issues.description: Prior memory conformity research shows that familiarity and relationship can affect conformity. The manuscript does not state whether dyads are strangers, acquaintances, couples, or how familiarity will be measured or controlled.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet."

issues.subcategory: age restriction does not eliminate age-status confound
issues.description: The age range of 16–35 still permits large age/status differences, such as a minor paired with an adult, which could affect discussion dynamics. No pairing rules or covariate measurement are specified.
issues.quote: "The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one"

issues.description: The study uses visual stimuli, polarized glasses, auditory podcasts, and a silent movie, but does not specify exclusion or accommodation criteria for visual impairments, color vision deficiencies, hearing impairment, language proficiency, neurological conditions, or prior familiarity with the stimulus materials.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old"

issues.subcategory: MORI manipulation awareness not checked before debriefing
issues.description: The MORI technique depends on participants believing they saw the same movie. Although participants are asked at the end about the study purpose, there is no explicit manipulation check for noticing different movie versions, polarized-glasses deception, or discrepancies during viewing/discussion. Awareness could invalidate the manipulation or moderate effects.
issues.quote: "are not aware that the other person is watching a different version"

issues.description: The intervention podcasts explicitly tell participants about memory fallibility, co-witness misinformation, and reliance on their own memory. These instructions may reveal the hypothesis and induce demand compliance rather than genuine resistance to conformity. The planned hypothesis-awareness question occurs only after the outcome and is described as exploratory, not as a control or exclusion criterion.
issues.quote: "The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner."

issues.subcategory: awareness construct not measured at item level
issues.description: The theoretical account hinges on participants being aware of discrepancies between their own memory and the partner's information, but the design does not measure discrepancy awareness, source memory, or item-level recollection of the partner's statements. This prevents testing the proposed mechanism and may obscure intervention effects.
issues.quote: "we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies."

issues.description: The extended warning includes memory education, source monitoring advice, confidence information, and enlightenment; education includes memory fallibility and possibly efficacy; demonstration and motivation includes DRM false-memory induction, feedback, legal consequences, and instructions. Because each condition bundles several ingredients, observed differences cannot identify which construct or mechanism caused effects.
issues.quote: "the following ideas were included ... a clear warning ... an extensive lecture ... information about the possibility of confusing sources ... information that many people ... remember the correct content ... an enlightenment"

issues.subcategory: DRM task may not operationalize social influence vulnerability
issues.description: The demonstration condition is theoretically based on resistance to social influence, but the DRM task demonstrates associative false recall, not co-witness social influence or misinformation acceptance. The operationalization may not match the intended construct of vulnerability to illegitimate social influence.
issues.quote: "The demonstration of the fallibility of memory will be done by means of the DRM technique"

issues.description: The authors claim normative influence is completely ruled out because the final test is individual. However, normative pressures can operate during the collaborative discussion, influence encoding of partner information, agreement, commitment, and later desire for consistency with a partner. The claim is too strong and overlooks social mechanisms active during misinformation exposure.
issues.quote: "we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study"

issues.description: The manuscript repeatedly attributes possible effects to abandonment of the consistency assumption, increased alertness, source monitoring, confidence, or motivation, but the planned design largely measures only final memory responses. Without measuring mediators, causal claims about mechanisms will be unsupported.
issues.quote: "we assumed that the extended warning would cause participants to abandon the consistency assumption, make them more alert to discrepancies ... and consequently cause them to rely on their own knowledge"

issues.subcategory: possible collaborative recall contamination not standardized
issues.description: The amount and quality of misinformation depends on each dyad's discussion, confidence, dominance, and whether the partner mentions the critical alternative. Although audio is recorded, the analytic plan does not model exposure dosage or conversational dynamics, which may differ by condition if interventions occur before discussion or by random dyad composition.
issues.quote: "Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer."

issues.subcategory: intervention may alter original memory rather than conformity
issues.description: If interventions are administered after discussion but before test, they may alter retrieval strategy, response criterion, confidence, or willingness to report, not memory conformity per se. If administered before discussion, they may alter the discussion and misinformation exposure. The design does not disentangle memory change, reporting criterion, and discussion behavior.
issues.quote: "Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity ... they will complete the individual memory test"

issues.subcategory: overall number of answers ambiguous in forced-choice format
issues.description: The authors plan an 'overall number of answers' index, but if the test is forced choice every item receives an answer unless 'don't know' is available; if open-ended, omissions vary. The outcome is not well defined and depends on the unresolved test-format contradiction.
issues.quote: "(4) the overall number of answers"

issues.description: For open-ended questions, the manuscript does not specify acceptable synonyms, spelling variants, partial answers, ambiguous answers, multiple responses, or 'don't know' coding. For forced choice, it does not specify alternatives, option order randomization, or whether 'don't know' is available.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions"

issues.description: The podcasts are described only generally. Full scripts, wording, examples, length, speaker, tone, and validation are needed because intervention content is the core manipulation and could strongly affect demand characteristics and outcomes.
issues.quote: "The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast about the fallibility of human memory."

issues.description: The DRM condition says four lists will be chosen based on previous research but does not provide the exact lists, presentation rate, recall interval, scoring method, or evidence that the lists reliably induce false recall in the target language/population.
issues.quote: "Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect."

issues.subcategory: ethical/debriefing and minor consent details missing
issues.description: Participants include 16- and 17-year-olds and the study uses deception about visual acuity and co-viewing. The manuscript does not describe consent/parental consent, ethics approval, deception justification, or safeguards for minors.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old"

issues.description: The only exclusion criterion is technical problems. No plan is provided for incomplete sessions, participant withdrawal, missing final-test responses, inaudible discussion recordings, failed intervention exposure, or missing confidence ratings. Missingness could be nonrandom and affect analyses.
issues.quote: "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session."

issues.description: 'Any technical problems' is broad and subjective, especially in a MORI setup where projection alignment, glasses use, audio recording, and visibility issues may vary. Without objective criteria and timing of exclusions, researcher degrees of freedom are substantial.
issues.quote: "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session."

issues.description: The plan lists multiple indices and average accuracies without identifying a single primary outcome for each hypothesis. This increases analytic flexibility and makes confirmatory interpretation difficult, especially for a registered-report style study.
issues.quote: "using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers"

issues.subcategory: hypothesized intervention ordering not linked to specific tests
issues.description: The authors predict Demonstration and motivation will be most effective, Extended warning next, and Education least effective, but the analysis plan only mentions omnibus interaction and pairwise comparisons. It does not specify a planned contrast for the ordered hypothesis.
issues.quote: "the Extended warning against misinformation is expected to be slightly less effective than Demonstration and motivation but more effective than Education about memory"

issues.description: The DRM predictor analysis and hypothesis-awareness analysis are described as exploratory but lack model specification, predictors, outcomes, exclusion rules, and correction for multiple testing. This creates room for undisclosed flexibility.
issues.quote: "As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique."

issues.description: Participants are 16–35-year-old volunteers recruited via media/internet, likely not representative of actual eyewitnesses, older adults, children, or diverse forensic contexts. The manuscript frames implications for justice systems but does not adequately constrain generalization.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet."

issues.description: The study uses a silent 6.5-minute film and artificial dyadic discussion under deception. Although MORI improves co-witness realism, this setting differs from high-stress, consequential, delayed, police-interview eyewitness situations. Broad claims about witness testimony and justice systems should be limited.
issues.quote: "the participants will watch a silent movie that lasts 6 minutes and 34 seconds"

issues.description: The manuscript adapts inoculation theory, which involves weakened attacks and refutational preemption, to a DRM false-memory demonstration plus legal-motivation podcast. The link to inoculation mechanisms is weak, and the intervention does not clearly train discrimination between legitimate and illegitimate co-witness memory influence.
issues.quote: "We adapted the ideas from the research described above in the hope that it may be useful in mitigating memory conformity."

issues.description: Participants rate confidence for each final answer, and the theoretical rationale emphasizes lack of confidence and reliance on external sources. However, confidence is not incorporated into the main analysis plan or mediator tests, missing an opportunity to evaluate the proposed construct.
issues.quote: "for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% ... to 100%"

issues.description: The manuscript states a total sample of 240 but does not explicitly state planned participants or dyads per condition, nor how unequal dyads/exclusions will be handled. Because randomization is by pair, condition-level dyad counts are central to power and analysis.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)."

issues.description: Random assignment helps balance memory ability across conditions, but with dyadic clustering and only 30 dyads per condition, imbalances in baseline memory, attention, or visual acuity may affect results. No baseline memory or attention checks are planned except the DRM task in one condition, which itself is part of the manipulation.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old"

issues.subcategory: possible confound from control podcast content
issues.description: A podcast on soft skills related to social attitudes could itself influence conformity, social agreement, or attitudes toward others, which are directly relevant to co-witness discussion and later reliance on partner information. It may not be an inert control.
issues.quote: "participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes"

issues.description: The manuscript refers to a 'significant main interaction,' which is statistically imprecise. More importantly, the analysis plan does not clearly distinguish the omnibus interaction, simple effects, and planned contrasts.
issues.quote: "In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed."

issues.subcategory: no preregistration/registered-report details despite confirmatory claims
issues.description: The manuscript appears to be a Stage 1 proposal and includes hypotheses, but it does not provide a complete preregistered analysis specification, including exact models, covariates, exclusion timing, coding rules, data transformations, alpha thresholds, and stopping rules. This undermines confirmatory status.
issues.quote: "If the Stage 1 review is accepted, the resubmission should be completed no later than in 2023."

issues.subcategory: causal language exceeds design for real-world outcomes
issues.description: The study can test immediate effects of interventions on laboratory memory reports, but the manuscript discusses preventing erroneous testimony and justice-system errors. It cannot establish effects on actual legal testimony, conviction errors, or long-term witness behavior.
issues.quote: "Due to the serious consequences of inaccurate testimonies, research on methods of reducing the memory conformity effect is extremely important for the proper functioning of justice systems."

issues.subcategory: planned use of ANOVA for mutually exclusive response categories
issues.description: Correct, misinformation-consistent, other, and omissions are mutually dependent categories. Running separate ANOVAs on each count ignores the multinomial structure and induces correlated tests; a multinomial or categorical mixed model would be more coherent.
issues.quote: "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers ... and (4) the overall number of answers."

issues.subcategory: order effects in final memory test unspecified
issues.description: The final test includes critical and filler questions, but the order, randomization, and whether discussed/non-discussed questions are intermixed are not specified. Question order may cue the manipulation or differentially affect retrieval.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details"

issues.subcategory: collaborative recognition test may cue critical alternatives
issues.description: During discussion, each question has five possible responses displayed. This recognition format may introduce additional misinformation beyond the partner's statements and can cue both correct and incorrect alternatives. The analysis frames misinformation as coming from the co-witness, but response options themselves may contaminate memory.
issues.quote: "Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer."

issues.description: Because the collaborative test displays multiple possible responses, any later misinformation-consistent answer may be due to option exposure rather than partner influence. This threatens the construct validity of 'memory conformity' as social influence from a co-witness.
issues.quote: "Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer."

issues.subcategory: collaborative test materials not fully described
issues.description: The manuscript does not provide the 12 collaborative questions, five response options, which four critical items are discussed, or how option order is determined. These details are essential to replicate the misinformation exposure.
issues.quote: "The test will comprise 12 questions, four of which refer to critical details ... with the other eight being control questions."

issues.subcategory: no assessment of actual attention to podcasts
issues.description: Participants listen to podcasts as interventions, but there is no comprehension or attention check. Differences in listening quality could add noise or bias, and null results could reflect failed exposure rather than ineffective interventions.
issues.quote: "Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast"

issues.subcategory: DRM feedback may fail for participants without false recall
issues.description: The demonstration condition assumes participants will falsely recall critical lures, but some may not. The feedback says 'If so, you were fooled,' meaning participants without false recalls do not receive a personal vulnerability demonstration. The intervention dose therefore varies systematically with memory performance, complicating interpretation.
issues.quote: "See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief. If so, you were fooled."

issues.description: No plan is given for participants who do not falsely recall any critical lures in the DRM condition. They may not receive the intended demonstration, yet will presumably remain in the condition, potentially diluting effects or creating unplanned subgroup analyses.
issues.quote: "The DRM procedure usually results in most of the participants falsely recalling at least a few of the critical lures."

issues.subcategory: contamination within dyads during interventions unclear
issues.description: The interventions appear to be administered to both members of the dyad together. For the DRM task and feedback, participants may see or infer each other's responses, creating additional social influence or embarrassment. The manuscript does not specify whether intervention tasks and final tests are completed privately.
issues.quote: "the participants will be asked to work on multiplication problems for five minutes. After that, the third phase will take place"

issues.description: The final memory test is individual, but the manuscript does not specify whether dyad members are separated, prevented from communicating, or seated apart. Privacy is necessary to remove direct social pressure and support the theoretical assumption about non-normative influence.
issues.quote: "they will complete the individual memory test of the original material"

issues.subcategory: incorrectly equating response accuracy with memory quality
issues.description: The manuscript often interprets final answers as memory accuracy or memory reports, but interventions may affect reporting criterion, willingness to guess, or compliance. Without source-memory measures or process dissociation, reduced misinformation-consistent responding does not necessarily imply improved memory.
issues.quote: "would reduce co-witnesses’ susceptibility to misinformation"

issues.description: Prior memory conformity effects may be large, and interventions may yield near-ceiling correct answers or floor misinformation responses with only four items per condition. The ANOVA plan does not address non-normality, boundedness, or ceiling/floor effects.
issues.quote: "the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation"

issues.description: The study uses Polish translations of instructions and materials, but only some materials are noted as translated. The podcast interventions, DRM lists, final memory questions, and collaborative options require validation to ensure semantic equivalence and comprehensibility.
issues.quote: "the instruction was translated into Polish by a native speaker"

issues.subcategory: possible sex/gender and dominance effects not addressed
issues.description: Memory conformity can be affected by interpersonal dominance, gender composition, and perceived credibility. The design does not mention measuring or balancing dyad gender composition, dominance, confidence, or credibility.
issues.quote: "always a pair of them"

issues.description: The manuscript does not describe compensation, recruitment quotas, participant source, or whether participants sign up alone or in pairs. These details matter because dyad familiarity and motivation can affect conformity.
issues.quote: "they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet"

issues.subcategory: sample size insufficient for small-to-medium interactions acknowledged but implications understated
issues.description: The authors acknowledge that 240 participants cannot detect small effects, but the interventions are novel and plausible effects may be small. Claims of efficacy or ineffectiveness, especially null effects, should be constrained; the analysis plan does not provide equivalence bounds or sensitivity analyses.
issues.quote: "this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes but not small ones."

issues.description: The sample size is set at 240, but the manuscript does not specify whether this is before or after exclusions, whether excluded participants will be replaced, or when data collection stops. This can affect power and analytic flexibility.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people"

issues.subcategory: timeline outdated or inconsistent with proposal status
issues.description: The timeline states that the study will be conducted in 2023 and resubmission completed no later than 2023, which is inconsistent with a prospective proposal if reviewed after that date. This raises uncertainty about whether data have already been collected and whether analyses are truly prospective.
issues.quote: "The study will be conducted in 2023. If the Stage 1 review is accepted, the resubmission should be completed no later than in 2023."

issues.subcategory: no data-quality criteria for MORI viewing
issues.description: The MORI method requires proper head position, glasses use, and image separation. The manuscript gives instructions but does not specify checks for peeking, head tilt, seeing both images, image brightness, or calibration criteria.
issues.quote: "Please make sure you watch the movie through the glasses (no peeking over the top or around the side)"

issues.subcategory: critical-item discussion options may create retrieval practice confound
issues.description: Discussed items differ from non-discussed items not only in misinformation exposure but also in retrieval practice, social elaboration, and recognition-option exposure. The within-subject comparison may confound memory conformity with retrieval practice effects, which could improve memory for discussed items or alter confidence.
issues.quote: "the participants will complete the collaborative recognition test ... participants will discuss half of the discrepant details"

issues.description: The design compares discussed to non-discussed items within the same participants but lacks a group with no collaborative discussion. This limits ability to separate conformity from item discussion/retrieval-practice effects and from general effects of the collaborative task.
issues.quote: "The correctness of answers to questions concerning discussed and non-discussed details will be compared."

issues.description: The extended warning is also a memory-fallibility lecture, while education about memory includes information about suggestibility and misattribution. The labels imply distinct constructs, but the operationalized interventions overlap substantially, weakening interpretability of between-intervention differences.
issues.quote: "Secondly, we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions"

issues.subcategory: unfalsifiable mechanism inference from overlapping interventions
issues.description: The authors acknowledge that equal results would not mean mechanisms are the same, but do not provide a design capable of distinguishing mechanisms. This weakens the theoretical contribution beyond a pragmatic comparison of packages.
issues.quote: "even if they produce the same results, this does mean that the mechanisms by which the were effective are always the same."

issues.subcategory: confidence ratings analysis omitted despite repeated continuous outcome
issues.description: Confidence ratings are collected but no statistical model is specified. Because confidence is central to the intervention rationale, omitting analysis or leaving it unspecified creates flexibility and reduces interpretability.
issues.quote: "participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer"

issues.description: Participants' guesses about the real purpose are recorded, but the manuscript does not specify coding procedures, reliability, whether aware participants are excluded or analyzed separately, or how this affects confirmatory conclusions.
issues.quote: "Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance."

issues.description: The extended warning and motivation conditions may induce suspicion about the partner or experimenter, which could reduce partner-consistent responses independent of memory monitoring or resistance to misinformation. The design lacks measures to distinguish suspicion, demand, distrust, and genuine memory accuracy.
issues.quote: "a clear warning that the partner might have been wrong during the collaborative recall"

issues.subcategory: accuracy on filler questions not theoretically integrated
issues.description: The plan says average accuracy on filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions will be observed, but filler items do not have co-witness misinformation status and are not integrated into hypotheses. This may become an exploratory outcome without clear construct meaning.
issues.quote: "Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions."

issues.subcategory: possible rehearsal and memory decay differences across conditions
issues.description: Because the Demonstration and motivation condition likely lasts longer than podcast conditions, the delay between collaborative recall and final test may differ by condition. Memory decay or interference from the DRM word lists could confound intervention effects.
issues.quote: "First ... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used ... Next, the participants’ motivation ... will consist in them listening to a podcast"

issues.description: The DRM word-list task is a memory task administered between the event and final test. It may interfere with memory performance or alter response strategies independently of demonstrating vulnerability, making it a confounded manipulation.
issues.quote: "It will consist of the participants listening to experimenter presenting lists of words from a common category"

issues.subcategory: open-ended versus forced-choice comparability to prior power estimates
issues.description: Power estimates for the conformity effect are based on prior MORI studies using forced-choice outcomes, but the manuscript also claims to use open-ended questions. Open-ended responses may yield smaller effects, lower guessing, and different variances, invalidating the power calculation.
issues.quote: "In existing research using the MORI technique a two-alternative forced-choice questions test was used as the main index of correctness of answers."

issues.subcategory: incorrect or unclear location of analysis plan as results
issues.description: The manuscript labels the section 'Analysis plan' rather than Results, but it is presented after Method and before data collection. The review task asks for locations among standard sections; more substantively, no actual results exist, so planned tests should be specified prospectively in sufficient detail. The current plan remains ambiguous.
issues.quote: "3. Analysis plan"
